claims.text: TaVCrW is initially a disordered BCC solid solution with possible short-range order.
Electronic excitations near the Fermi level are relevant in TaVCrW.
The proposed method replaces EAM with a DFT-trained MTP and replaces thermodynamic integration with free-energy perturbation.
MTP plus FEP will reduce computational cost by more than 80% relative to TOR-TILD.
The proposed method will agree with the baseline to within 0.5 meV/atom.
Accurate reproduction of the ab initio solid and liquid phase-space distributions by the MTP is the mediator enabling FEP to replace TI.
In TaVCrW, SRO changes the VDOS and produces high-frequency optical-band structure.
The enthalpic cost of disrupting SRO, represented by ΔH_DAPB, increases kink-pair formation energy.
The ΔH_DAPB contribution is a structural mediator governing the convergence or bias of FEP.
SRO stabilizes TaVCrW by approximately 2-3 meV/atom.
A supercell larger than approximately 200 atoms is sufficient to resolve the relevant SRO clusters.
Sampling at 2000-2400 K captures the phase-space distribution relevant to melting and SRO in TaVCrW.
An accurate MTP captures the complex solid and liquid energy landscapes sufficiently well for unbiased FEP.
FEP bypasses the slow convergence and extensive sampling required by TI when the reference potential reproduces the target distribution.
Electronic excitation effects shift the predicted TaVCrW melting point.
High-temperature magnetic fluctuations can materially alter the alloy free-energy landscape.
The usual GGA-PBE/LDA underbinding and overbinding rules fail for V and Cr at 0 K.
The TOR-TILD baseline using EAM and TI is computationally expensive.
The benchmark is falsified if the MTP+FEP and TOR-TILD free-energy results differ by more than 0.5 meV/atom or if cost reduction is below 80%.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis and predicted outcome describe melting-temperature accuracy using the energy unit meV/atom, whereas the falsification rule applies 0.5 meV/atom to a free-energy difference. Melting-temperature agreement requires a temperature unit or an explicit conversion through the free-energy slope.
The conditions suggest that a supercell larger than 200 atoms is sufficient, while the uncertainty field states that the required supercell size is not defined and requires empirical validation.
